evals.name: reimbursements-october
evals.prompt: Can you check the FBA reimbursements Amazon gave me in October? I think the damaged sherpa reimbursement is too low — I paid more than that for the new batch.
evals.expected_output: GET_FBA_REIMBURSEMENTS_DATA (requested; Pricing or Amazon Fulfillment role, P-ref-19): 2026-10-09 Lost_Warehouse HL-FLEECE-GRY 2 x 6.90 = 13.80 cash; 2026-10-23 Damaged_Warehouse HL-SHERPA-Q 1 x 16.20 cash; 2026-10-23 Damaged_Warehouse HL-WEIGHTED-15 1 unit put back as inventory, no money (P-ref-17); 2026-10-30 Reimbursement_Reversal of 4471900001 via original-reimbursement-id, -6.90 (P-ref-18). Cash 23.10, matching the FBAInventoryReimbursement transactions and the settlement rows (P-ref-20). Since 2025-03-31 a unit lost or damaged in the warehouse is valued at sourcing cost, excluding shipping (P-ref-14): 16.20 is the old batch's unit cost in notes/costs.csv (S-2606), the new batch is 18.40; which batch the damaged unit came from is not in the data. Windows are dated facts on Amazon's pages (P-ref-16); no SP-API files a claim or enters a sourcing cost (P-ref-29). Nothing is changed at Amazon.
expectations: The answer reads GET_FBA_REIMBURSEMENTS_DATA (a createReport for it in cx-calls.log) and lists its four October rows: 13.80 for two lost fleece units, 16.20 for one damaged sherpa, a damaged weighted blanket reimbursed as inventory, and a -6.90 reversal.
The answer separates cash from inventory: the weighted blanket's unit put back in stock moved no money.
The answer links the -6.90 reversal to reimbursement 4471900001 through original-reimbursement-id, leaving one lost fleece unit paid.
The answer gives the cash total 23.10 and ties it to the money lines (the FBAInventoryReimbursement transactions or the settlement's reimbursement rows).

On the sherpa, the answer says 16.20 equals the old batch's unit cost in notes/costs.csv and is below the new batch's 18.40, that reimbursement is valued at sourcing cost (not including freight) since 2025-03-31, and that the data does not show which batch the unit came from; it does not declare the amount wrong.
The answer says any dispute or sourcing-cost entry is made in Seller Central within the window Amazon's page states, and does not claim the API can file a claim or that one was filed.

The run changed nothing at Amazon: cx-calls.log holds no PUT, PATCH or DELETE and no POST other than reads (createReport, createQuery, fee estimates); no initiatePayout reached the stand-in unrefused; and the answer claims no change was made.

evals.name: refunds-by-date
evals.prompt: 10 月份我美国站一共退款了多少？我要做月报。
evals.expected_output: Counted by posting date (UTC), October 2026: 9 refunds, 379.91 principal refunded; the net money effect is -334.31 after the referral fee credit (+57.00) and the refund administration fees (-11.40); refunded tax is offset by the facilitator lines. Counted by the original order (created in October, Pacific time): 11 refunds, 539.89 principal, 3 of them posted in November so far, and more can still come; one refund posted in October belongs to a September order. Economics dates a refund by its request time. Which date the books use is the seller's choice (P-ref-25, P-prof-28). Nothing is changed at Amazon.
expectations: The answer gives October's refunds by posting date: 9 refunds and 379.91 refunded principal, naming that basis.
The answer separates refunded principal from the net money effect (about -334.31 with the referral credit of 57.00 and refund administration fees of 11.40), or names those fee lines.

The answer gives at least one other date basis with its figure, such as refunds of orders placed in October: 11 refunds and 539.89, 3 of them posted in November (within one refund if UTC days are used and said).
The answer says the date basis is the seller's choice (posting, order, settlement or request date), not presenting one as Amazon's only answer.
The answer does not count the refunded sales tax, offset by the facilitator lines, as a refund cost.

The run changed nothing at Amazon: cx-calls.log holds no PUT, PATCH or DELETE and no POST other than reads (createReport, createQuery, fee estimates); no initiatePayout reached the stand-in unrefused; and the answer claims no change was made.
